title: The Hidden Downsides of Noise-Canceling Headphones
text:
Noise-canceling headphones have several benefits, but there are also some downsides to consider. Users may develop habits that are detrimental to the headphones or their own well-being, and noise cancellation can have unintended consequences.
Noise-canceling headphones have several benefits, but there are also some downsides to consider. One issue is that users may develop habits that are detrimental to the headphones or their own well-being.
For example, when using active noise-canceling (ANC) headphones, users may feel the need to crank up the volume to overcome higher-frequency ambient noise. This can degrade perceived sound quality and lead to inner ear injuries over time.
Additionally, constantly using ANC can cause the battery to drain up to 50% faster, reducing the lifespan of the headphones. Furthermore, noise cancellation can make ambient noise sound muffled or further away, which can be more dangerous than complete noise cancellation. To mitigate these risks, users should consider taking breaks from their noise-canceling headphones and using transparency mode while out and about. This can help keep users aware of their surroundings and prevent potential hazards
